<pre>
cd ~/claude
gh repo clone terrenceb-atlnz/device-testing     # or: git clone git@github.com:terrenceb-atlnz/device-testing.git
</pre>
''First time only: clone into <code>~/claude/</code> in your lab home, because the testboxes run the tools from <code>~/claude/device-testing/</code>. Then follow the repository's <code>README.md</code> one-time setup. Its memory-link step matters.''

''How to run a list of test cases on lab hardware with Claude Code's <code>/test-mode</code> skill, and how to turn the results into the files you attach in Zephyr with <code>/create-logs</code>. Owner: Terrence Beach. Last updated: 22 October 2026. On that date it was checked against these files in the <code>device-testing</code> repository: the <code>test-mode</code>, <code>create-logs</code>, <code>orient-dt</code> and <code>wrap-dt</code> skills, the <code>bench-runner</code> agent, the sentinel kit, <code>bench_probe.py</code>, <code>logged-output.md</code>, <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code>, <code>MANUAL-ONLY.md</code> and <code>tools/README.md</code>.''

'''<code>/test-mode</code>''' runs a list of test cases on '''any testbox you name''' as one supervised campaign:
# It asks about the box: which testbox, which consoles, the PDU, and any constraints.
# It checks that nobody else is using those consoles.
# It measures the bench with the facts you gave it. Then it reports which cases the bench can run and exactly what blocks the others.
# It runs the cases the bench can run. For each case it keeps a working log, saves each device's config and adds a line to a '''results list'''.
# You review the results. Then you run '''<code>/create-logs</code>''', which builds the files you upload: one <code>.log</code> plus the <code>.cfg</code> files for each case.
A watchdog called the ''sentinel'' keeps the run moving. It also passes messages between you and the tester.

This page is part of the [[Ask-ck]] tooling. Ask-CK's Test Composer turns a test case into a <code>.setup</code> + script pair. <code>/test-mode</code> runs those scripts, and the device-testing campaign cases, on hardware. Ask-CK can also start a campaign itself; see [[#Campaigns started by Ask-CK]].

On this page, '''the Test Engineer''' means you, whoever invokes the skill. Nothing assumes a particular person, testbox or product. <code><TB></code> is your testbox and <code><FAMILY></code> is the DUT's product family. '''tb470''', '''IE520''' and '''x960''' appear only as marked examples.

== At a glance ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Question !! Answer
|-
| What does it do? || It takes a list of case IDs or titles and sorts them into groups. It checks that the bench can run each case, runs the cases it can, and keeps a results list with one verdict per case.
|-
| Which bench? || '''Any testbox you name''' at the start. It uses '''only the consoles you list''' and leaves every other console on the box alone.
|-
| How many Claude sessions? || '''One.''' The session you type into becomes the sentinel. For each group of cases it starts a tester (the <code>bench-runner</code> agent) as a background sub-agent.
|-
| Will it ask me questions? || Yes, at the start: testbox, consoles, PDU, constraints, and whether the run will take several hours. After triage it asks one more: proceed now, or reconfigure the bench first? After that it asks only about things that are yours to decide, including any disagreement between your facts and the bench.
|-
| Will it change what I told it? || '''No.''' Your answers are recorded word for word and never overwritten. If the bench or a record disagrees with one, it asks you which is right.
|-
| What if someone else is on the box? || It checks ''before'' it opens any console. If anything holds your consoles, or might, it stops and shows you what it found. It never displaces anyone.
|-
| Can it change device config? || Yes, within a test: config, <code>write</code>, reloads and DUT power cycles, on your consoles and your PDU outlets only. It restores what it changed. Bench-level changes stay with you: recabling, applying a new <code>.setup</code>, root on the testbox, licences.
|-
| What does every case check? || The case's own steps, plus a '''DUT health check''' before and after (reboots, exceptions, log, CPU, memory). Traffic cases are graded on crafted frames, not on ping. See [[#What every case checks]].
|-
| Who decides the verdict? || The tester grades each case. You review the results list and can re-grade any case until the final logs are made.
|-
| When are the final logs written? || '''Only when you run <code>/create-logs</code>''', after your review. <code>/test-mode</code> and <code>/wrap-dt</code> never write them. (An Ask-CK campaign is the one exception.)
|-
| Where does the output go? || One folder per case in the <code>device-testing</code> repository: <code><TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/</code>. See [[#Where everything is written]].
|-
| Does it upload anything? || '''No.''' You attach each case's <code>.log</code> and <code>.cfg</code> files to the case in Zephyr (Jira).
|-
| Does it push to GitHub? || No. It commits. Company permissions deny <code>git push</code> to Claude every time, so you push.
|-
| How do I resume after a crash? || Run <code>/test-mode --resume</code>. The queue file and the per-case commits are the resume point.
|}

== Before you start ==

# '''Start Claude Code in the repository root''' (<code>claude/device-testing/</code> in the lab home). The session loads its memories according to the directory it starts in. A session started anywhere else loads the wrong memories, or none.
# '''Have your answers ready''' for the setup questions: the testbox, your consoles, the PDU's IP and outlets, and anything special about this session.
# '''For a run of more than an hour, start it inside <code>tmux</code>.''' See [[#Running long campaigns: use tmux]].
# '''SSH and Python are handled for you.''' Every step on the box goes through the <code>tools/tb</code> wrapper. It sets the SSH keyring agent and picks a Python of 3.7 or newer on the box (tb101, tb105 and tb277 use <code>python3.8</code>). If SSH fails, see <code>TESTBOX-ACCESS.md</code> §0.
# '''The box's deployed <code>.setup</code> must be reachable''' at <code>/home/st-art/st-art/configs/<TB>.setup</code>, unless the box has none yet. Example, tb470: after a reboot <code>/nfsHome</code> can be unmounted, and the <code>.setup</code> then looks missing although the file is intact. Re-mounting needs root (<code>sudo mount /nfsHome</code>), so you do it.
# '''The deployed <code>.setup</code> must describe the bench as it is now.''' If units, cabling or console speeds changed since the last <code>apply</code>, the probe reports MISMATCH. Every case that depends on what moved then waits until you run <code>apply</code>. If you know the bench changed, run <code>/orient-dt</code> first and decide about <code>apply</code>.
# '''Optional: set your dev host's default box.''' Add one line for your own host to <code>bench-setup/default-boxes</code>: <code><hostname> <tbNNN></code>. Never edit another user's line. <code>/test-mode</code> always asks for the box and offers the one it finds. <code>/orient-dt</code> and <code>/wrap-dt</code> choose a box in this order: the box you name; else your last recorded test bench run; else your host's line; else '''SKIPPED''' (no box touched).

== Invoking it ==

<pre>
/test-mode T24032 T12067                 # case IDs
/test-mode 33235, "Fixed port speed"     # IDs, titles, or a mix
/test-mode --resume                      # continue the newest campaign queue
/test-mode --resume <TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md   # continue a specific queue
</pre>

With no list and no <code>--resume</code>, it asks for the list and stops.

== The setup questions ==

The sentinel asks these together, before it touches any box. Each one accepts free text, and the sentinel offers the obvious options.

{| class="wikitable"
! Question !! What to give !! Why it matters
|-
| '''Testbox''' || <code>tbNNN</code>. It offers the box from your last recorded run or your host's <code>default-boxes</code> line, and always "Other". || Selects the box's files and where the output goes.
|-
| '''U interfaces''' || The <code>/dev/uN</code> consoles this session uses, and what is on each if you know (e.g. <code>u2,u4,u5 = stack; u3 = DUT2</code>). || '''Only these are ever probed or opened.''' Every other console belongs to someone else.
|-
| '''PDU''' || The PDU's IP and the outlet for each console (e.g. <code>u2=6, u3=8</code>), or "no PDU / do not power-cycle". || The probe writes this into the <code>.setup</code>'s power section. With no PDU, the framework's power cycle after a failed case silently does nothing, so that is recorded too.
|-
| '''Session constraints''' || e.g. "shared box: read-only probe, log out of consoles", a time window, devices or cases not to touch, the box's lab segment, who else uses the box. '''Optional:''' ask for reboot-heavy cases to be held until after office hours, if the noise of repeated PDU cycles would disturb people nearby. || Constraints can tighten the standing orders. They never loosen anything marked '''always'''.
|}

If the run is long (more than a handful of cases, or reloads, failovers or long observation windows) and you are in the VS Code editor, it then asks the '''multi-hour''' question. See [[#Running long campaigns: use tmux]].

All the answers go into a '''Session facts''' block at the top of the campaign's queue file, word for word and dated. Its first line is <code>Test Engineer: <whoami>@<hostname></code>. That line is how <code>/orient-dt</code>, <code>/wrap-dt</code> and <code>/create-logs</code> later find "your last test bench run". On <code>--resume</code> the sentinel asks only for facts the queue does not have, plus a one-line "still the same?" check.

== What happens, step by step ==

{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Step !! Who !! What you see
|-
| 1 || '''Setup questions''' || Sentinel → you || The questions above. It also reads <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code>, <code>TESTBOX-ACCESS.md</code>, the general traps in <code>/orient-dt</code>, and <code>platforms/<FAMILY>.md</code> for the DUT. If the family has no platform file, the triage report says so.
|-
| 2 || '''Multi-hour?''' || Sentinel → you || If yes and you are in VS Code, it explains the risk and offers to stop so you can restart in <code>tmux</code>.
|-
| 3 || '''Write the queue file''' || Sentinel || <code><TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md</code> holds your session facts, a Queue table (one row per group), an empty Results table and an Issues list. It is committed before anything runs, because '''it is the resume point'''.
|-
| 4 || '''Occupancy check''' || Sentinel (read-only SSH, '''no console opened''') || '''CLEAR''': it carries on. '''FOUND''': it stops and shows you what it found. See [[#The occupancy check]].
|-
| 5 || '''Arm the sentinel''' || Sentinel || One line: armed, which mode, where the live feed file is, and how to switch modes.
|-
| 6 || '''Probe and triage''' || Tester (mode TRIAGE) || The tester repeats the occupancy check, then probes ''your'' consoles with ''your'' PDU facts. You get the triage report word for word: '''N runnable / M blocked by topology, each with the exact change that unblocks it / K blocked by something else'''. Cases listed in <code>MANUAL-ONLY.md</code> are reported as MANUAL-ONLY. A USER-CONFLICT, MISMATCH or NEEDS-CHECK comes back to you first; see [[#When your facts and the bench disagree]].
|-
| 7 || '''Proceed or reconfigure?''' || You || ''Proceed'': the runnable cases run, and the rest are marked BLOCKED with their reason. ''Reconfigure'': you make the change (recable, destack, <code>apply</code>) and say "done". Triage then runs again with a fresh check and probe.
|-
| 8 || '''Run''' || Tester (one sub-agent per group, mode RUN) || For each case the tester commits the <code>.cfg</code> files and working log, then sends a <code>RESULT</code> line. You see '''one line''' per case, e.g. <code>T12589 FAIL -- <reason>  (3/12: 2 PASS, 1 FAIL)</code>, plus short running updates.
|-
| 9 || '''Completion''' || Sentinel || The final results list and the blocked rows. It ends with ''"please run /create-logs after reviewing the results for the final uploadable product."'' and stops. See [[#At the end of a campaign]].
|}

Nothing runs on the bench between groups, so that is the cheapest time to recable for a blocked group. The sentinel tells you when one is pending, and triages that group again before it runs. Before each dispatch it also repeats any topology gap from triage ("cases X need Y; fit Z first or accept UNSUPPORTED"), because a gap mentioned hours earlier is easily forgotten.

== The occupancy check ==

Before anything opens a console, the box is checked for anything that holds your consoles or could compete for them. The check sends '''nothing''' to any console, not even a carriage return:

<pre>
tools/tb precheck <TB> <U-list>          # from the repo root on the dev host
</pre>

It looks at:
* '''each of your consoles''': who holds the <code>ttyUSB</code> device behind <code>/dev/uN</code> (<code>fuser</code>, with <code>sudo -n</code> where passwordless sudo works), and its lock files;
* '''the whole box''': every <code>screen</code>, <code>tmux</code>, <code>minicom</code> or <code>picocom</code>-type process and every running Python script, whoever owns it. For a root-owned <code>sudo minicom</code> it finds the person who started it;
* '''who is logged in''' (<code>w</code>), for information.

The results:
* '''CLEAR''' (exit 0): the probe may run.
* '''FOUND''' (exit 5): the sentinel '''stops and returns to you''' with the list: which console, which process, which user, how long it has been up. It never kills, detaches or displaces anything. Run it again when the console is free, or narrow your list to the free consoles.
* '''UNKNOWN counts as FOUND.''' Without passwordless sudo, a root-owned <code>sudo minicom</code> is invisible and looks exactly like a free console.
* '''Idle is not free.''' A minicom that has been open for hours is still someone's console.
* An SSH failure is reported the same way. It is never worked around.

The tester repeats the check immediately before every probe it runs, because time has passed.

== When your facts and the bench disagree ==

The probe gets your session facts (<code>--pdu</code>, <code>--outlet uN=…</code>, and <code>--name uN=…</code> if you gave names) and uses them for that run.
* A unit that the box's facts file (<code><TB>.static</code>) does not list yet is '''added''' with your facts.
* A recorded line is '''never rewritten'''.
* When your fact disagrees with the record or the bench, the probe reports a '''USER-CONFLICT''' (exit 4). Examples: you said outlet 7 for u2 but the record says 6; or you gave facts for a console where no device answered.

Triage stops, and the sentinel asks you about each conflict, e.g. ''"The session says PDU outlet 7 for u2 (S/N …); the record says 6. Which is right?"''
* '''Your session fact is right:''' with your go-ahead, that one line of the facts file is changed, with a dated note naming you.
* '''The record is right:''' the queue's Session facts block is corrected, and you are told.

Nothing is changed on either side without your answer. Triage then runs again.

The other probe results:
{| class="wikitable"
! Exit !! Meaning !! What happens
|-
| 0 MATCH || The bench matches the deployed <code><TB>.setup</code>. || Triage, or the run, goes ahead.
|-
| 1 MISMATCH || The bench does not match the template. || Triage works from what the bench ''is'', and you see the diff. In a run, cases that depend on what moved do not start; the others carry on. <code>apply</code> is your decision.
|-
| 2 NEEDS-CHECK || Something could not be verified: a NIC with no carrier, a MAC not learned, a console busy or silent. || Shown to you. It is yours to resolve.
|-
| "no template" || The box has no deployed <code>.setup</code> yet. || The generated <code>bench-state.md</code> is the only description of the box. Writing the template (<code>apply</code>) is yours.
|}
The tester never "fixes" the bench or a record to make a check pass. MATCH does not mean healthy: the probe's Advisories block can still flag problems, and the tester reads it.

== Where everything is written ==

Everything a campaign produces goes in the <code>device-testing</code> repository under '''<code><TB>/<FAMILY>/</code>'''.
* <code><STAMP></code> is the campaign's start time, local, <code>YYYY-MM-DDTHHMM</code>. All its groups share it.
* <code><id></code> is the case ID without its prefix (<code>38472</code> for AWPTCM-T38472).
* <code><dev></code> is a device's name in the box's <code>.setup</code> (e.g. <code>stk_a</code>, <code>swi_b</code>).

<pre>
<TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md               the queue and the results list: the resume point
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<TB>-<consoles>.setup   the run .setup: only the units this group uses
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/<dev>.cfg          one per device, saved after setup (a deliverable)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/work/run<N>.log    the tester's working log, one per run of the case
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/work/…             this case's own scripts, captures, health samples
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/<id><suffix>.log   the final log                    (only /create-logs)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/<id>-review.md     the case's process review        (only /create-logs)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/README.md               the group's verdict table        (only /create-logs)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/REVIEW.md               the group's process review       (only /create-logs)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/SESSION-HANDOVER-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md        the session handover             (/wrap-dt)
</pre>

Example: <code>tb470/x230v2-28GS/ports-2026-10-09T0845/47208/</code>.

* '''During the campaign''' a case folder holds its <code>.cfg</code> files and <code>work/</code>. '''After <code>/create-logs</code>''' it holds its one <code>.log</code>, its <code>.cfg</code> files and its <code><id>-review.md</code>.
* A case that was never attempted (NOT TESTED) gets no folder. The results list carries the reason.
* Raw console transcripts stay on the box (<code>/tmp/<run>/console-<uN>.log</code>) and are never committed.
* Reusable helpers go in the repo-root <code>tools/</code>, never in a case folder. See [[#Helper tools]].
* The rules for all of these files are in <code>logged-output.md</code> at the repo root. If this page and that file differ, that file is right.

The box's own measured state is in <code>bench-setup/<TB>/</code>: <code>bench-state.md</code>, <code><TB>.static</code>, <code><TB>.setup.current</code>, <code>captures/</code> and <code>backups/</code>. tb470 is the exception: it keeps the same files directly in <code>bench-setup/</code>. The deployed template is <code>/home/st-art/st-art/configs/<TB>.setup</code> on the box.

'''Older campaigns stay as they are.''' Before 2 October 2026 the logs were flat (<code><group>-<STAMP>/<case-id>.log</code>), and on tb470 before 1 October they were under <code>IE520/<group>-<date>/</code>. They are not rewritten, and <code>/create-logs</code> does not regenerate them.

== Verdicts and the results list ==

Every attempted case gets exactly one verdict. '''The tester grades it''', and you may re-grade it during review. The final log's name carries the verdict:

{| class="wikitable"
! Verdict !! Final log !! Meaning
|-
| PASS || <code><id>.log</code> || The case ran, and every step the platform supports passed. UNSUPPORTED steps inside it do not prevent a PASS. '''Only a PASS uses the plain name.'''
|-
| FAIL || <code><id>-fail.log</code> || The case ran and a check failed, or the platform prevented it from running.
|-
| PARTIAL || <code><id>-partial.log</code> || The case could ''not'' run fully (a physical or other misconfiguration, a script error, a manual step nobody did), and no FAIL condition was met.
|-
| UNSUPPORTED || <code><id>-unsupported.log</code> || The platform does not support what the case tests.
|-
| NOT TESTED || no folder, no log || Never attempted. The results list carries the reason.
|}

In short: a platform gap is UNSUPPORTED, a bench or script gap is PARTIAL, and a case nobody attempted is NOT TESTED. A product feature that the product's specification (TPS) says is supported but the DUT lacks is a finding, not a limit. The full definitions are in <code>logged-output.md</code> §1.

'''The results list''' is the <code>## Results</code> table in the campaign's queue file, kept by the sentinel. It has one row per case with the columns ''case, title, group, verdict, reason, working log, graded''. ''graded'' is <code>tester</code>, or <code>Test Engineer, re-graded from <VERDICT> on <date></code>. You review this table, and <code>/create-logs</code> builds from it.

== What every case checks ==

These are standing orders. They apply to every case, on every testbox, whoever runs it.

* '''The DUT's health, twice''' (<code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> §8, from 19 October 2026). Once before step 1 and once after the last step, the tester reads <code>show reboot history</code>, <code>show exception log</code>, a filtered <code>show log</code>, <code>show log tail 150</code> (after only), <code>show cpu</code> and <code>show memory</code>. One <code>tools/tb health</code> call takes each sample, and the second call compares it with the first and says CLEAN or DIRTY.
** A new reboot nobody caused, an exception, or a kernel or crash line makes the run '''confounded'''. The case keeps its step verdict, and the tester tells you with a <code>NEEDS TEST ENGINEER:</code> note. Re-running is your decision.
** The framework's own power cycle after a failed case shows as <code>Unexpected System reboot</code>. It is matched against the run's power-cycle lines before it counts as a finding.
** One case can never prove a memory leak. It can only show a rise that did not come back after teardown.
** <code>/create-logs</code> refuses to finish a case whose log has no health block.
* '''Traffic is tested with crafted frames, not ping''' (<code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> §7, from 15 October 2026). The tester builds the exact frame the feature acts on, sends a known count, and counts what arrives. It also sends a '''control''' flow that the feature must ''not'' act on, in the same run. A verdict rests on that pair. Ping proves only that a link or path is up.
* '''A baseline with the feature off''', when the case changes behaviour (STEP 0 in the final log).
* '''The DUT's <code>show system</code>''', captured in full in each case's own setup reads. The final log quotes it.
* '''Tidy configs.''' Each case's additions are removed, and the removal is proved by a diff of the running config against the copy taken before the case. Nothing is written to startup config unless the case needs it.
* '''Only the units the run uses.''' The tester binds a run <code>.setup</code> that lists only the units the group uses. The framework's power cycle after a failed case then never reboots a unit the case did not touch. The deployed <code>.setup</code> is never edited for this.

== How the sentinel works ==

The sentinel is '''mandatory''' for any session that runs tests (standing order, 28 September 2026). It has two jobs:
* '''Rescue:''' it notices a tester that has stalled or stopped early, and gets it going again.
* '''Channel:''' you talk to the sentinel, which is never busy with the bench, so you never wait for a tester to finish. It relays your directions to the tester, and the tester's questions to you.

In <code>/test-mode</code> the sentinel is the session you type into. '''It never opens a console''': it sends no console bytes, no config and no device login. Two writers on one console is the classic failure, so the sentinel only passes facts, and the tester does the work.

=== Its parts ===

{| class="wikitable"
! Part !! What it is !! Lifetime
|-
| '''Watcher''' (<code>sentinel.sh</code>, run by a Claude Code ''Monitor'') || A shell loop that wakes every 30 s and makes '''one''' SSH call to the box. It reads only the new bytes of the console transcripts and framework logs, and never opens a console. On the dev host it also reads the sub-agents' transcripts and background output. || A Monitor expires after 30 min, and the sentinel re-arms it each time. Read positions are saved, so nothing is missed or repeated.
|-
| '''Narrator''' (<code>narrate.sh</code>, Claude Haiku) || Turns each active 30-s tick into one '''<code>UPDATE</code>''' sentence, or an '''<code>ATTENTION</code>''' line when something needs a look (a FAIL, an error, a traceback, a power cycle). This keeps the sentinel's own conversation small: before it existed, one automated run woke the sentinel 331 times and cost $35. || Runs inside the watcher. If it fails, the watcher prints <code>NARRATOR DOWN</code> once and falls back to plain line counts.
|-
| '''Backstop''' (a cron trigger every 15 min) || Wakes the sentinel even if the watcher has died. It classifies the tester as healthy, needing you, or stalled, and acts. || Lives in this session only: '''closing the session kills it'''.
|-
| '''Completion notifications''' || A sub-agent that finishes, or stops early, notifies the session that started it. || This is the main stall signal.
|-
| '''Brief''' (a filled-in template in the session scratchpad) || The sentinel's orders for this campaign: testbox, consoles, tester name, queue file, stand-down time, mode. || Never committed.
|-
| '''Stand-down time''' || A hard stop for the watcher. The default is the end of your working day; the sentinel asks if you did not say. || The watcher exits at that time.
|}

=== Normal and verbose modes ===

{| class="wikitable"
! Mode !! What the sentinel is shown
|-
| '''normal''' (default) || One <code>UPDATE</code> sentence per active tick, <code>ATTENTION</code> lines, and the rescue alarms.
|-
| '''verbose''' || Normal, plus the raw console bytes, the tester's narration, every command it runs and its output, and the framework's other logs.
|}

* '''Switch at any time''' by asking the sentinel. No re-arm is needed.
* Every line the watcher prints wakes the sentinel and costs tokens, so output is capped at 40 lines per source per tick.
* The '''full verbose feed is always written''' to <code><scratchpad>/sentinel.feed</code>. For a free live view, run <code>tail -f</code> on it in your own terminal. That costs nothing, unlike running the sentinel in verbose for hours.

=== How it talks to you ===

* '''Healthy ticks are silent''', apart from one short line per <code>UPDATE</code>.
* '''Each finished case is one line.''' The sentinel checks the tester's <code>RESULT</code> line against the working log, then adds it to the Results table and commits. If the two disagree, or the log is missing, the row is still written with the mismatch noted, and you are told. The sentinel does not choose a side.
* '''You can re-grade at any time.''' Say e.g. "12589 is a PASS". The Results row changes, is marked as re-graded by you, is committed, and is confirmed in one line. The working log is not edited.
* '''When the tester needs you''', the sentinel shows it under a bold '''NEEDS YOU:''' header, with a running list of everything still unanswered. Remote Control is disabled by company setting, so '''the session text is the only channel'''. Check back on long runs.
* Your answers are relayed as "Test Engineer's answer, relayed: …", and your directions ("stop after this case") as "Test Engineer's instruction, relayed: …". The sentinel relays only what you said. It never answers for you.
* A new fact mid-campaign (another console, a corrected outlet) goes into the queue's Session facts with the time, is relayed, and is used by the next probe.
* The sentinel batches its messages and adds "no reply needed", because a tester often stops right after answering one.

=== Detached long runs ===

A soak test can run for many hours with no tester on the bench: a sampler (<code>tools/longrun.py</code>) records progress on the box, and the queue row reads <code>RUNNING-DETACHED</code>. Watching it every 30 s would waste tokens: a 12-hour run cost 125 million cache-read tokens for 13 useful reads. So while the row is detached, the sentinel:
# stops the watcher and the 15-minute backstop;
# sets one cron check per sample, timed just after each sample is written. Each check is read-only and silent when healthy;
# keeps a one-time trigger for the final phase, at the end of the run plus 5 minutes.
A dead sampler, a skipped or failed sample, a stack that is not in normal operation, or a traffic rate of 0 is shown to you under '''NEEDS YOU:'''. The watcher and backstop are armed again when the final phase's tester starts.

== What the tester does ==

The tester is the '''<code>bench-runner</code>''' agent, started by the sentinel as a background sub-agent. Every dispatch carries one mode and a '''session block''': testbox, consoles, PDU, outlets, names, constraints, session directory and stamp. It refuses a dispatch without one.

Every step it takes on the box goes through '''<code>tools/tb <action> <TB></code>'''. It never builds an SSH command by hand. It also has a reading budget of about 40,000 characters before the first case. It reads by section, not whole files, because everything it reads is paid for again on every later call.

=== TRIAGE ===

Read-only, apart from the bench probe.
* It runs the gate below, then checks every case's cabling needs against the measured bench with an offline preflight of each script.
* It reports N runnable / M blocked by topology / K blocked otherwise. Each topology block comes with the exact change that removes it: which port to cable to which, which device to add or move, which outlet to record, which unit to destack. A case is never "fitted" to the bench by weakening what it checks.
* It reads '''<code>MANUAL-ONLY.md</code>''', the tracked list of cases and steps that need a person (to watch an LED, hold a magnet on a fan, click through a GUI, supply an account or insert a USB stick). Those are reported as MANUAL-ONLY and never scheduled into an unattended run. A new one found at triage is added to the list, dated.
* It changes no device state and runs no case.
* '''A USER-CONFLICT stops triage''' and goes straight back to you.
* A second TRIAGE after a recable means a fresh occupancy check and probe. It never trusts the earlier capture.

=== RUN ===

One group of queue rows per dispatch. '''Before the group's first case''' it writes the group's bench setup and its exact restore recipe into the queue file and commits them, so that a fresh tester can restore the bench if this one dies mid-group.

'''The pre-run gate''', before every run:

{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Check !! If it fails
|-
| 1 || '''Occupancy check''' on your consoles (no console opened). || FOUND goes to you word for word. It '''never displaces''' anyone. A framework run it finds is someone's test, not drift.
|-
| 2 || '''No console is left in a root shell''' (from a killed run) '''or in config mode.''' || It records the state in the working log, then exits it.
|-
| 3 || '''The box's template path resolves.''' || Yours: fixing it needs root.
|-
| 4 || '''The bench matches its template''', measured with your facts (read-only on a shared box; at your console speed if you gave one). || MISMATCH or NEEDS-CHECK: dependent cases wait and the diff goes to you; the rest carry on. USER-CONFLICT: it stops and hands you the conflicts.
|-
| 5 || '''The run binds a run <code>.setup</code> cut from this box's''', listing only the units the group uses (or the topology pair Test Composer pre-loaded). || Does not launch.
|-
| 6 || '''Offline preflight''' of the script against that <code>.setup</code>. A missing cable otherwise looks like a script defect. || The case is BLOCKED by topology.
|-
| 7 || '''Every device boots its baseline config''' (e.g. <code>flash:/tb470-bench.cfg</code> on tb470), checked before and after. || Fixed within the test, or reported.
|-
| 8 || Ask-CK's server run path still carries the agreed run flags. || It launches by hand instead.
|-
| 9 || '''A sentinel is watching.''' || It refuses to start the first case.
|-
| 10 || '''The script's defaulting commands are valid on this platform.''' One rejected command fails every TestCase at step 1, and the framework then power-cycles every unit after each failure. || Does not launch; reports a script defect.
|}

Then, for each case:
* '''Runs framework scripts with <code>--noupdate --nodefaultcfg</code>''', always. Without them the framework rewrites every boot config, strips licences, reboots everything and tries to load firmware from the box's <code>/tftproot</code>.
* '''Has full authority within the test''': config, <code>write</code>, boot config, reloads, a PDU power cycle of a DUT, test traffic from the box's NICs, and scratch in the box's <code>/tmp</code>. That covers '''your consoles and your PDU outlets only''', within your constraints. It asks nobody, and '''it restores what the case changed.'''
* '''Saves one <code><dev>.cfg</code> per device''' after setup and before step 1: the running config, headed by three <code>!</code> lines naming the device, the case and run, and the box and console. '''A stack is one device with one <code>.cfg</code>''' (the master's).
* '''Writes <code>work/run<N>.log</code> as it goes''': the session facts, devices and links, every command with its prompt, the raw output that proves each step, the tools used and their arguments, both health samples, and the teardown diff. It labels the run ''clean'' or ''confounded'' and ends with a <code>VERDICT:</code> line. A re-run starts <code>run<N+1>.log</code>. The full list is in <code>logged-output.md</code> §2.
* '''Drives consoles only through <code>tools/console.py</code>''' and the tools built on it, with transcripts at <code>/tmp/<run>/console-<uN>.log</code> on the box, where the sentinel watches. A console driven any other way is invisible to the sentinel.
* '''Stops on any <code>%</code> error line''' from a device, and checks each dependent step against proven state.
* '''After the run''': on each console it sends <code>end</code>, then <code>terminal no monitor</code> (on a shared box it also logs out). It probes again with the same facts (expecting MATCH), compares each device's running config with the pre-run copy, and stops anything it started.
* '''Commits the case folder''', then sends the sentinel <code>RESULT <id> <VERDICT> -- <reason> -- <group>-<STAMP>/<id>/work/run<N>.log</code> and carries on.
* '''Never writes the final log or the group README''', and never deletes <code>work/</code>.
* '''Hands back''' when the group is done or every remaining row is BLOCKED, with verdicts, working-log paths and commit hashes. If it stops for any other reason, it says exactly which row is next.

'''Not the tester's to decide''' (<code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> §4):
* anything that contradicts your session facts;
* a console outside your list, or a holder the occupancy check found;
* licences (a case that needs a feature the unit lacks is UNSUPPORTED, not a licence request);
* a box you do not own or have not been given;
* applying a new <code>.setup</code>, or leaving the standing topology changed;
* root on the box (keys, sshd, routes, firewall rules, mounts, device trust);
* writes outside the three repositories;
* traffic beyond the box's own lab segment (e.g. tb470's is <code>10.38.215.0/24</code>; for another box, what your constraints say).

For these it writes the need in the working log, sends the sentinel one line starting <code>NEEDS TEST ENGINEER:</code>, and '''carries on with the next runnable case'''. It never waits at a prompt.

== At the end of a campaign ==

{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Step !! Who !! What happens
|-
| 1 || '''Results list''' || Sentinel || When every group is DONE or BLOCKED, it shows the final results list (verdict, reason, graded-by and working log for each case), the counts by verdict, and the BLOCKED rows with the change each still needs. It ends with ''"please run /create-logs after reviewing the results for the final uploadable product."'' and stops. It stays armed so you can still give directions.
|-
| 2 || '''Review and re-grade''' || You || Read the list, open any working log you want to check, and re-grade anything you disagree with. Re-grades go in the Results table, never in the working log.
|-
| 3 || '''<code>/create-logs</code>''' || You run it || Builds the final output from what is committed. Details below.
|-
| 4 || '''Attach in Zephyr''' || You || Attach each case's <code>.log</code> and <code>.cfg</code> files to the case in Zephyr (Jira). '''No tool uploads anything.'''
|-
| 5 || '''<code>/wrap-dt</code>''' || You run it || Stands the sentinel down, restores what the session changed, probes the bench again, writes the dated session handover, commits, and reports how many commits are waiting for you to push. It never writes or edits a case log. If you wrap before <code>/create-logs</code>, the handover lists the cases that still need it.
|}

Steps 3 and 5 can happen in either order, and in different sessions.

=== /create-logs ===

<code>/create-logs</code> turns a reviewed campaign into the files you attach in Zephyr. It runs '''only when you ask''': run it, or say "create the logs".

<pre>
/create-logs                                              # this session's campaign, else your newest one
/create-logs <TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md       # a specific campaign
/create-logs <TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md 24032 # only some cases of it
</pre>

It runs in the sentinel session or any later session started in the repo root. '''It never touches a testbox.''' It uses only what is committed: the Results table, each case's <code>work/</code> folder and its <code>.cfg</code> files.

'''What it does, in order:'''
{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Step !! Detail
|-
| 1 || '''Reconcile''' || Checks every Results row against the folders. A case that already has its final log and no <code>work/</code> is skipped, so running it twice is safe. A case with <code>work/</code> but no Results row is left alone and listed.
|-
| 2 || '''Confirm once''' || Shows the table it will build from and anything that did not reconcile, then asks: ''Yes, create them'' / ''Re-grade first'' / ''Not yet''. '''It never re-grades by itself.''' A verdict that looks wrong to it is named for you to decide.
|-
| 3 || '''Write each final log''' || <code><id><suffix>.log</code>, from the template in <code>logged-output.md</code> §4, using the '''latest run only'''. When single TestCases of a framework TestSet were re-run, each re-run result replaces the earlier one, so the TestSet keeps one clean log.
|-
| 4 || '''Check the <code>.cfg</code> files''' || Every device in the log's topology needs its <code><dev>.cfg</code>. A missing one is named to you. It is never invented.
|-
| 5 || '''Check the tools''' || A helper that exists only in <code>work/</code> is moved into <code>tools/</code> with a <code>tools/README.md</code> entry.
|-
| 6 || '''Check every final log''' || The name's suffix matches the verdict; the header is complete; <code>Build:</code> quotes <code>show system</code> in full; '''a sourced <code>HEALTH:</code> block is present'''; every STEP has a verdict; the wording is plain English; nothing mentions an earlier run, another campaign, the sentinel or <code>work/</code>. A case that fails a check keeps its <code>work/</code> and is listed for you.
|-
| 7 || '''Write the group <code>README.md</code>''' || One line (testbox, DUT, dates) and a verdict table with every case of the group, NOT TESTED included. It is rewritten in full each time.
|-
| 8 || '''Review the process''' || Measures each case's token use from the tester's transcript (<code>tools/case_tokens.py</code>) and writes <code><id>-review.md</code> per case and <code>REVIEW.md</code> per group: wasted input, repetition, accuracy risks, and what the next run should reuse (expected outputs per step, scripts, references). These reviews are for you and the next tester, not for Zephyr. The next tester reads their "Next run" sections.
|-
| 9 || '''Clean up and commit''' || Deletes <code>work/</code> only for cases that passed step 6. One commit per group. It never pushes. The working files stay in git history.
|-
| 10 || '''Report''' || The table of final logs, the token table with the three biggest savings, anything skipped or failing a check, any claim left out for lack of a source, the commit hashes, and ''"The logs and .cfg files under <TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/ are ready to attach in Zephyr."''
|}

'''What a final log contains''' (template: <code>logged-output.md</code> §4):
* A header: Run (one short sentence), Bench, Tester, Graded, Case, Build (the DUT's full <code>show system</code>), Configs.
* The <code>VERDICT:</code> line and what was proven, then the block for that verdict:
** FAIL: <code>FAIL CONDITION:</code> (and <code>TRIED:</code> when there was more than one attempt);
** PARTIAL: <code>NOT RUN:</code> and <code>UNBLOCK:</code>;
** UNSUPPORTED: <code>NEEDS:</code> and <code>ABSENT:</code>.
* <code>CAVEAT:</code>: what the run did not establish.
* <code>HEALTH:</code>: one line each for reboots, exception log, log, CPU and memory, before and after.
* TOPOLOGY AS TESTED: an ASCII diagram of what the case used, then the devices, serials, consoles, links, host NICs and tools. With the <code>.cfg</code> files, it is enough to rebuild the case.
* One STEP block per step: commands with their prompts, the raw output word for word, short notes on the lines that matter, and a closing <code>=> STEP n <VERDICT>:</code> line.

'''Each run stands alone.''' A final log never mentions earlier runs, other campaigns, setup detours or conversations; those stay in the working log, the review and the handover. Device output is copied exactly from the working log. A claim with no source in the working log is left out and named to you. That is why the tester's working log records more rather than less.

'''Written for every reader.''' The text is checked as if read by a junior engineer whose first language is not English: one idea per sentence, common words, no idioms, numbers rather than adjectives.

== Campaigns started by Ask-CK ==

Ask-CK can start a campaign itself (<code>/test-mode --from-ask-ck <hand-off file></code>). Only Ask-CK's launcher passes that option, and the skill refuses it unless the hand-off file exists. The queue's Session facts then carry a <code>Driver: ask-ck (<run id>)</code> line, and these differences apply:

* '''It never stops to wait.''' Where a user-driven campaign would ask you something, it prints a <code>NOTIFY</code> line, which Ask-CK's server turns into an email, and works past the problem. If it cannot, it marks that case BLOCKED and moves on. It still never makes a decision reserved for you (root, <code>apply</code>, recabling, licences, a USER-CONFLICT, displacing a console holder).
* '''Results appear in Ask-CK.''' The sentinel prints the marker lines Ask-CK reads: <code>RESULT</code>, <code>NOTIFY</code>, <code>PROBE</code>, <code>REPAIRED</code>, <code>REVIEWED</code>, and <code>ASKCK-DONE</code> at the end. Running updates go to Ask-CK's page, not to the session. Re-grading happens in Ask-CK's results table.
* '''Final logs are automatic''', for manual cases only: the sentinel runs <code>/create-logs --auto</code> with no confirmation, and keeps <code>work/</code> until the results are accepted in Ask-CK. A script case's framework log is already its final output.
* '''Kinds of run''' (from the hand-off):
** <code>composer-validate</code>: triage only. It probes the bench against a template and prints <code>PROBE MATCH|MISMATCH|NEEDS-CHECK</code>.
** <code>validation</code>: one script. The tester repairs a '''copy''' of the script until it runs cleanly end to end, changing mechanics only (imports, timing, console handling, a rejected defaulting command), never a check. It stops after 5 unclean runs. Each change is logged in <code>work/repairs.md</code>. The sentinel then reviews the logs and the script against the case's steps (<code>review.md</code>). The framework's verdict stands.
** <code>scripts</code>: validated scripts run in the order you ticked them. A failing script does not stop the run.
** <code>composer</code>: a normal triage and run.

'''A user-driven <code>/test-mode</code> is unchanged''': it asks you, and it never writes final logs by itself.

== Helper tools ==

Reusable helpers live in the repo-root '''<code>tools/</code>''' (about 70 of them), catalogued in '''<code>tools/README.md</code>''' with how to run each one and what it was verified on.

* '''<code>tools/tb</code>''' is the one way a session reaches a testbox: <code>tools/tb <action> <box> [args]</code>. It sets the SSH agent, picks the box's Python, passes login passwords over stdin (never on a command line other users can see), and refuses to open a console another process holds. <code>tools/tb --help</code> lists the actions.
* The catalogue covers:
** console drivers, a CLI answerer, and a help probe that never executes the command (<code>qmark</code>);
** the per-case health check (<code>health</code>) and a two-console link tester (<code>speedrow</code>: speed, duplex, link-up time and LLDP, both ends from one process);
** reload, flash-copy, TFTP-copy and Boot Menu helpers;
** running-config diffs and host inventory;
** scapy traffic senders and counters, line-rate UDP, pcap builders, flow and loop windows;
** protocol emulators and wire decoders: IGMP, IPv6 ND/RA, DHCP/DHCPv6, DNS, LLDP/LLDP-MED, LACP, RADIUS, SNMP, sFlow, NTP, HTTP, RESTCONF, Modbus;
** IXIA chassis control (<code>ixtcl</code>) and a detached long-run sampler (<code>longrun</code>);
** <code>ckcase</code> (look up a case in Ask-CK's database by its AWPTCM ID) and <code>case_tokens</code> (token use per case).

The rules for the tester, and for you if you write a tool:
# '''Look in <code>tools/README.md</code> first.''' Use or extend what is there; never write a second tool for the same job.
# '''Write it generic.''' Testbox, consoles, NICs, ports, VLANs and addresses are arguments, never constants. If it works on only one platform, its README entry says so.
# '''Commit it with its <code>tools/README.md</code> entry''', in the same commit as the case that first needed it.
# The working log names the tool and its exact arguments, so that the run can be repeated.

Only a script that truly belongs to one case (with its ports and VLANs written in) stays in that case's <code>work/</code>, and <code>/create-logs</code> deletes it with the folder.

== Recovery: what the sentinel can and cannot rescue ==

{| class="wikitable"
! What goes wrong !! How it is noticed !! What happens !! What is lost
|-
| The tester stops early ("Next: running T931" and then nothing). This is the most common failure. || Completion notification || The sentinel compares the report with the queue and the case folders, then continues the ''same'' sub-agent: what completed, the exact next row, "no reply needed". || Nothing.
|-
| The sub-agent has gone (finished, crashed, out of context) with rows left || Completion notification, or the IDLE alarm || A fresh RUN dispatch for the remaining rows. Its gate probes the bench again first, and the group's restore recipe in the queue says how to get back to a clean state. || At most, the case in progress.
|-
| The tester is waiting on something that can never happen (e.g. an SSH <code>pgrep</code> loop that matches itself; one ran for 14.6 h) || IDLE alarm after 300 s with no activity, flagged '''STALL SIGNATURE''' || The sentinel tells the tester what actually completed and where to resume. || The idle time.
|-
| The tester needs you || A <code>NEEDS TEST ENGINEER:</code> message || Shown under '''NEEDS YOU:''', and your answer relayed back. Only the blocked case waits. || Nothing.
|-
| Someone starts using one of your consoles mid-campaign || The tester's occupancy check before its next probe || It stops before that run and sends you the FOUND list. || The wait.
|-
| The watcher is killed (editor or VPN drop, 30-min expiry) || Expiry notification, or the 15-min backstop finds no watcher || Re-armed: it removes '''this session's''' stray watchers, clears the heartbeat and arms again. Nothing is repeated or missed. || Nothing.
|-
| The usage window runs out mid-campaign || The backstop fires after the window refreshes || It continues, or dispatches again, from the first row not DONE or BLOCKED. || The wait.
|-
| '''The session's process dies''' (window closed, editor reload, xrdp or VPN drop) || Nothing in the session notices: the sentinel, its cron and the sub-agent all die together || '''You''' start a session in the repo root and run <code>/test-mode --resume</code>. || The case in progress.
|}

On <code>--resume</code> the new session:
# reads the queue file and its Session facts, and confirms them with you;
# reconciles the Results table with the case folders (a committed working log ending in a <code>VERDICT:</code> line gets its missing row);
# runs the occupancy check;
# says which row is next;
# arms the sentinel again and continues.

Before resuming, check that the old session is really gone (<code>ps</code>). Two resumed copies means two testers on one console.

The sentinel '''cannot''' fix the bench, decide a bench-level question for you, or lift a mechanical block. The no-stray-scripts hook, the auto-mode safety classifier and the company <code>git push</code> denial do not change because a message was relayed. Those come back to you.

=== Running long campaigns: use tmux ===

The tester lives inside the session's process, so if that process dies, the campaign stops until someone resumes it.
* A VS Code window is exposed to editor reloads and connection drops.
* A bare terminal is no safer: closing it sends SIGHUP.
* A terminal inside <code>tmux</code> (or <code>screen</code>) survives a closed window or a dropped connection:
<pre>
tmux new -s test-mode
cd <lab home>/claude/device-testing
claude
/test-mode <cases>          # re-attach later with:  tmux attach -t test-mode
</pre>
In an unattended session, put any step that may raise a permission prompt last. One unattended session waited 11 hours on a prompt after its run had finished.

For a tester that must outlive its sentinel, the older '''two-session shape''' is still supported: one session runs the cases and a second watches it (<code>/orient-dt</code> §10).

== Shared testboxes ==

Most testboxes are shared by ST-ART framework runs, people on minicom, and other Claude sessions.

=== Someone holds a console ===
* The occupancy check finds them before any console is opened, and the sentinel stops and tells you. The tester's own gate catches anyone who starts later. Neither ever logs in on top of someone.
* If a console still reads busy during the probe, the probe skips it and reports '''NEEDS-CHECK''', so no run that needs it starts.
* Say "shared box" in your constraints. The probe then runs read-only: logins and <code>show</code> commands only, no LLDP switch-on, no MAC-learning pings. The tester logs out of every console it opened.
* On a box you do not own, ask its users before probing, even when the check is CLEAR. The check shows who has a console open ''now'', not who owns the bench.

=== An ST-ART framework run is in progress ===
* Its signs are a stack hostname like <code>stk_a_<test>_<run></code> and <code>[SCRIPT]</code> lines in the device log. That is someone's test, not drift. Nothing should "restore" it.
* Between steps it may hold no console and look idle. Check the time of the last <code>[SCRIPT]</code> line before sending traffic: two runs on one bench corrupt each other's results.

=== Another Claude session on the same bench ===
* '''Run one campaign per set of consoles at a time.''' Two testers configuring the same devices collide, and nothing in the tooling prevents it. Sessions on ''different'' consoles of a box are fine if their cases share no devices or cabling.
* Your console feed shows every transcript under the box's <code>/tmp/*/</code>, so another session's console traffic appears in it.
* The IDLE alarm counts '''any''' <code>python3</code> or <code>tcpdump</code> on the box as a live job, so another user's job can hide a stalled tester. Completion notifications are unaffected.

=== Two /test-mode sessions on the same dev host ===
* This now works (fixed 21 October 2026). Each session removes only its own stray watchers, so the two no longer kill each other's.
* '''They share one git working tree.''' Every session on the host commits in the same NFS checkout. Each session commits only its own files. <code>/orient-dt</code> and <code>/wrap-dt</code> pause peer sessions before they sync with GitHub.

== Notes ==

* '''Standing orders apply to every Test Engineer.''' <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> holds the bench owner's standing answers. Your session constraints can tighten them for a session, and a queue file can add overrides for one campaign; neither can loosen anything marked '''always'''. The logging rules are in <code>logged-output.md</code>.
* '''Power cycles after failed cases are accepted.''' After a TestCase that ends FAIL, UNSUPPORTED or ERROR, the framework power-cycles every unit in the run <code>.setup</code> (about 4 minutes for six units). Nothing works around this. A script that fails every case at the same defaulting step is stopped after two failures in a row. These cycles show as <code>Unexpected System reboot</code>, one per failed case, all in the same minute.
* '''Budget time generously.''' Example, IE520: copying a release into SPI flash takes about 12 minutes for 41 MB, and the unit answers nothing meanwhile. It looks crashed; never power-cycle it then.
* '''Bench setup changes once per group, not between its cases.''' Cabling, aggregators, VLAN isolation and boot pointers are set before the group and restored after it. A case that needs a different physical setup belongs in a different group.
* '''Legacy hand-written suites have three extra traps''' (seen with T24032 on tb470, 2 October 2026):
** their TestSet powers '''off''' every device it did not initialise, so partner units go dark: turn the outlets back on and probe again before the next case;
** they hard-code test VLAN IDs and delete them in teardown: check them against the bench's VLANs before launch, and remap a clash in a copy of the script, never on the bench;
** the framework console wraps at 80 columns, so a one-line <code>show log</code> match can miss a long line: read the raw device log before grading such a step FAIL.
* '''The probe is the bench's source of truth.''' <code>bench-state.md</code> is generated by <code>bench_probe.py run</code> and never edited by hand. The <code>.setup</code> on the box is written only by <code>apply</code>, which is your decision. The names-and-outlets file (<code><TB>.static</code>) is yours; the probe only adds new units to it.
* '''History is in git, not in the output.''' Each run keeps its own <code>work/run<N>.log</code> until <code>/create-logs</code>. The final log and the <code>.cfg</code> files describe the latest run only.
* '''Nothing is pushed.''' Every commit is reported as "committed, NOT pushed". You push. <code>/orient-dt</code> and <code>/wrap-dt</code> report how many commits are waiting.
* '''Skill and agent changes need a new session.''' The skills and the <code>bench-runner</code> definition are read when a session starts.
* '''Framework run directories under <code>/tmp/ck*/</code> are not watched''' by the default feed, which watches <code>/home/st-art/pytest-create/</code>. A tester that runs elsewhere needs an extra Monitor.
* '''A rejected or interrupted tool call can still be running on the box''', holding a console or changing config. The tester checks <code>ps</code> and the consoles after any interruption.
* '''Never send <code><command> ?</code> followed by Enter''' through a console driver: if <code><cr></code> is a valid completion, the command runs. <code>tools/qmark.py</code> asks for help without running anything.
* '''<code>terminal monitor</code> and <code>terminal no monitor</code> work only at the exec prompt''', and <code>terminal monitor</code> does not toggle. The console tools handle this. A console driven by hand needs <code>end</code> first.
* '''Each password is sent once.''' AW+ locks an account after 5 failed logins, and every failure restarts the 5-minute lock. The console tools never retry a password.
* '''Platform limits give UNSUPPORTED, not FAIL.''' Triage says in advance which cases they affect. Each product family's facts are in <code>platforms/<FAMILY>.md</code> (e.g. <code>platforms/IE520.md</code>, <code>platforms/x960.md</code>), which <code>/test-mode</code>, <code>/orient-dt</code> and the tester read. A family with no file yet is worked from the general traps.

** <code>.claude/agents/bench-runner.agent.md</code>: the tester and its gate.
** <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code>: the standing orders every Test Engineer works under.
** <code>MANUAL-ONLY.md</code>: cases and steps that need a person at the bench.
** <code>tools/README.md</code>: the catalogue of reusable helpers, starting with <code>tools/tb</code>.
** <code>platforms/<FAMILY>.md</code>: each product family's limits and traps.
** <code>bench-setup/bench_probe.py</code>: <code>precheck</code>, <code>run</code>, <code>apply</code>.
** <code>.claude/skills/orient-dt/SKILL.md</code>: §0a git sync, §0b which bench, §4 framework traps, §10 and <code>.claude/skills/orient-dt/sentinel/</code> the sentinel procedure and kit.
** <code>.claude/skills/wrap-dt/SKILL.md</code>: ending a session.
** <code>TESTBOX-ACCESS.md</code>: SSH access and launching framework runs.
